claims.text: The Dependency Inversion Principle: high-level modules should not depend on low-level modules; both should depend on abstractions.
claims.source_hint: glossary entry dip; standard formulation in software design literature

claims.text: PlaceOrderSplit.Notify(int customerId) calls Console.WriteLine($"sending an email to customer {customerId}") directly; nothing in PlaceOrderSplit.cs references INotifier.
At stage-0, the only code referring to INotifier outside its own file is NotifierBase, which implements it.
INotifier declares void Send(int orderId, string subject); EmailNotifier and SmsNotifier derive from NotifierBase, which implements INotifier, and each overrides Format with its own message text.

A C# method or constructor parameter typed INotifier accepts an instance of any class implementing INotifier (implicit reference conversion), so callers can pass EmailNotifier, SmsNotifier or a new implementation without the receiving code changing.
claims.source_hint: C# conversions: implicit reference conversion from class to implemented interface

claims.text: High-level code that creates new EmailNotifier() itself is tied to EmailNotifier even if it stores the result in an INotifier variable.
claims.source_hint: outline item 3; coupling definition from design.l1.coupling-and-cohesion

claims.text: DIP concerns the direction of dependencies; the mechanism that creates concrete objects and passes them in is a separate topic (next module).
EmailNotifier.Format holds the email's fixed format ("email about order {orderId}: {subject}"); the subject text is passed in by whoever calls Send.
